feed.title: Re: RFC: Two years of BIP Editing, time for some new faces?

entry.title: Re: RFC: Two years of BIP Editing, time for some new faces?
entry.summary:
The current workload for the BIP Editor team has become increasingly unsustainable, with several high-quality submissions remaining unreviewed for extended periods. Despite additional support from non-editors in reviewing new BIPs, the backlog continues to grow, particularly when team members are unavailable due to travel or time off. This situation has led to a persistent struggle to keep up with the volume of open work, even as significant personal effort is invested into managing the BIPs repository.
To address these challenges, two main strategies have been identified. One option involves increasing the number of active BIP Editors to better distribute the workload and ensure timely reviews. The alternative would require lowering editorial standards, such as forgoing comprehensive reads of new submissions in favor of focusing solely on formatting requirements. However, there is a clear preference for strengthening the editorial team by appointing three active BIP Editors who can consistently contribute to daily operations.
Flexibility in commitment length is also considered important. Potential volunteers are encouraged to consider limited terms of service, such as 12 to 24 months, rather than feeling pressured to make indefinite commitments. This approach aims to attract qualified candidates who might otherwise hesitate due to concerns over long-term obligations.
